apps.name: catalog
apps.title: catalog
apps.description: A store for a repository of Holm apps: a page for every app, and a sheet that installs it on your node.

listing.subtitle: A store for app repositories
listing.description:
The store you're looking at. It lists every app in a repository of Holm apps, gives each one its own page with screenshots, ratings and reviews, and the prompt that built it, and installs it on your node from a Get button.

Sign in to review an app; reviews appear once an admin approves them. The node's owner and admins get an admin page to show or hide apps, see how often each is viewed and installed, approve reviews and pick the store's colour.

It reads the repository's index.json, the same file a node reads from a repository it trusts. Point it at your own repository to give your apps a store of their own.
listing.whatsNew: PROMPT.md records the request that branded Holm's sign-in page.

screenshots.alt: The front page: a featured app and the list of all apps, each with a Get button
An app's page in dark mode: icon, rating, facts and screenshots
Ratings and reviews on an app's page, with a button to write one
The install sheet, with the terminal commands written for your node
The admin page: apps with their numbers and a switch to show or hide each one

apps.prompt:
Make this repository installable app by app, and build a catalog for it as a
Holm app. Use https://holmhq.com/llm.txt as your only Holm reference.

- Each top-level folder with a manifest.json is an app. Give each a version.
- Write scripts/index.mjs (Node, no dependencies). It writes index.json at
  the root: one entry per app with its name, path, version, a release tag
  named <app>/v<version>, and h1, a fingerprint of the files Holm would
  deploy, computed like Go's dirhash.Hash1 (as in go.sum). With --check it
  fails if index.json is out of date or an app changed after its version was
  tagged; with --tag it tags new versions.
- Run the check in CI, and tag new versions on main.
- In catalog/, build a page that reads index.json from GitHub on the server
  and shows each app with every way to install it on my node: clone and
  deploy, `holm app install` (not in Holm yet), and a prompt for a coding
  agent. Trusting the repository is one command, `holm app repo add`. Let me
  enter my peer and domain once, so every command fits my node.
- Deploy it to unofficial.<my-domain>.

apps.name: feedback
apps.title: feedback
apps.description: A button for your website, a QR code for your tables or event. Count the scans, read every word.

listing.subtitle: Feedback for websites, shops and events
listing.description:
Put a feedback button on your website with one script tag, or a QR code on your tables, counter or event badges. People send praise, problems and ideas from their phone, with a photo in one tap and a star rating if you ask for one.

Make it yours: your logo, cover, colour and words on the form, a button that eases in and opens into a panel that springs up, light or dark to match your visitors. A live preview shows every change on a stand-in page, and your site picks it up with the same snippet.

Everything arrives in one inbox per project, ready for hundreds of items: sort it, and filter it by status, time, kind, rating, site or any answer. Keep a thread of notes for your team, see where the button is live, and count how many people scanned, visited and sent something.
listing.whatsNew: Room for hundreds: your projects in a calm panel with each one's site and icon (pick from 48, or keep the random one), and an inbox that sorts by newest, votes or rating and filters by when, where and who can get a reply. Fifty at a time, with a count, a Clear, and / to search.

apps.prompt:
Build an embeddable feedback and issue tracker as a Holm app. Use
https://holmhq.com/llm.txt as your only reference for Holm.

- One script tag adds a feedback button to any website. It opens a small
  form: bug, idea or question, a message, and an optional email. Send the
  page's address along, without its query or fragment.
- Signed-in people make a project per site, with its snippet, a choice of
  button text, colour and position, and a live preview.
- An inbox per project: statuses (new, planned, in progress, done, closed),
  private notes, and where each item came from.
- An optional public board per project showing only the items I choose, with
  upvotes.
- Keep spam out without a captcha. Make it look good on mobile and desktop,
  light and dark.
- Deploy it to feedback.<my-domain>.

apps.name: pastebin
apps.title: pastebin
apps.description: Private-first text, code and media pastes with expiring links and burn-after-read sharing.

listing.subtitle: Links that expire or burn
listing.description:
Paste text, code or files and share them behind a link that expires, opens only once, or can be revoked at any time.

Code is highlighted as you type. Markdown renders like GitHub's, and images, video and audio play in place. Your name stays off the paste unless you choose to show it.

API keys and a small command-line tool let scripts and agents file pastes for you.
listing.whatsNew: PROMPT.md records the request behind the sign-in branding notes.

screenshots.alt: Writing a paste: highlighted code, and a create button that reads as a sentence
A Markdown paste rendered with headings, emphasis and lists
A TypeScript paste in dark mode, with line numbers and a fuse showing when it expires
A one-time paste, sealed until the reader chooses to open it

apps.prompt:
Build a pastebin as a Holm app. Use https://holmhq.com/llm.txt as your only
reference for Holm, and read its app-building sections before you write code.

- Make it really aesthetic, with light, dark and system themes.
- The UX should be excellent on mobile and desktop.
- Highlight syntax.
- A paste can hold text and media: images, video, audio or any file.
- Every link can expire, open only once, or be revoked by me.
- Hide my name on shared links by default; let me choose to show my name and avatar.
- After I sign in, let me create API keys, so scripts and agents can create
  pastes over HTTP. Include a small CLI.
- Deploy it to pastebin.<my-domain>.
